_comment: THE SINGLE HOME FOR EVERY ASSERTED CONSTANT.
ARCHITECTURE.md 11.1 requires that a gate which passed because it examined
zero files has not passed. Every gate therefore asserts a minimum quantity
of work done, and every one of those quantities lives HERE -- once.
Consequence, which is the entire point: a legitimate change to the engine
is a visible one-line diff in this file, reviewed on its own merits. A gate
can never be weakened silently, because weakening it means editing a number
here where a reviewer will see it.
Comparisons are EXACT EQUALITY, not >=. Adding a wrapper must be a
deliberate bump of this manifest, not something that slips through.
TWO CONTINUITY CONSTANTS, AND ONLY TWO. n_legacy_nodes and n_legacy_cards
describe the contract retired on 2026-08-21 and are read from
legacy-inventory.json. They must never move, because a continuity constant
that drifts was never one.
EVERYTHING ELSE HERE IS A MEASUREMENT of the tree as it stands, and moves
with it. n_nodes, n_categories and n_cards describe the LIVE catalogue;
engine.methods tracks the same catalogue, because the pyright, deptry and
interrogate floors have to scale with what actually exists. n_parity_cases
and n_recommend_fixtures count frozen oracles, so they do not move in
practice -- but they are measured from the artifacts, not promised.
THE VALUE "unmeasured" IS A HARD FAILURE, NOT A PLACEHOLDER. It marks a
constant whose measuring artifact does not exist in the tree yet. assert.sh
fails loudly and names it. A gate that cannot start must never look like a
gate that passed -- so this reads red until the artifact lands and the real
figure replaces the word, in a reviewed one-line diff.
Every value below is reproduced by the command beside it in
'commands', run from the engine directory. Never edit a number without
running its command first.

engine._comment_invocation_payloads: THE ONE CONSTANT IN THIS MANIFEST THAT WAS DELIBERATELY OWED, AND THE FIRST EVER TO CARRY THE WORD. It no longer is, and the history is kept here because the reason it retired is not the reason decision A4 wrote down. Box 2.1.14 double-runs a method and compares the bytes, and a method cannot be run without arguments to run it with. parity-fixtures.json holds argument-adapter VERDICTS, not call arguments, and node-specs.json declares argument KINDS, not values. So the method leg of that gate enumerates the implemented set and refuses to go green while skipping any member of it, which meant the first wrapper body written in 2.2 would turn it red unless it arrived with a call. WHAT THIS CONSTANT COUNTS IS ONE HALF OF WHERE THAT CALL COMES FROM, and reading a green gate as evidence about this figure is a mistake the original phrasing invited. The gate takes a UNION: a file under engine/tests/payloads/, which the command below counts, and an admissible oracle case under engine/tests/oracle/, which it does not. HOW IT ACTUALLY RETIRED: the first body, run_binomial_fe_glm, landed reached by its ORACLE CASE. A4 anticipated that -- the word does not retire itself the moment the double-run gate goes green -- and the decision taken here was to build engine/tests/payloads/ with an underscore-prefixed readme and nothing else, which makes the command below return a measurement instead of erroring, so the constant is a measured 0 and not an absent one. WHAT THAT MOVED, AND IT MOVED BETWEEN CI JOBS RATHER THAN DISAPPEARING. While the word stood, assert-inventory's OWED branch carried a coverage guarantee as a side effect: it refused to print OWED once ANY method carried a body, so the assert-inventory job in ci.yml answered for 'every implemented body has a call'. With a directory present that branch is not taken and assert.sh only compares a file count, so assert-inventory no longer answers for it. The guarantee is now carried in the engine-suite job, by tests/controls/double_run.py, which prints 'UNRUN <method>: no oracle case and no payload file' and exits non-zero. That is a stronger check than the one it replaced -- it names the method rather than the manifest word -- but it is a DIFFERENT JOB, and anyone reading a green assert-inventory as proof of call coverage would be reading the wrong gate. THE DEFINITION IS COMMITTED AND IS NOT IN THIS FILE: engine/tests/controls/double_run.py carries it in its module docstring -- the payload's shape, where the file goes, what produces it, what was rejected and why, how the harness consumes it, and why an admissible oracle case already IS an invocation payload and is reused rather than copied. It lives there because that module is what prints the red line, so the contract is in the file the person who meets the gate already has open. THIS FIGURE RISES only when a payload FILE lands, which is owed by the first body that has no oracle case to be reached through.
engine._comment_unresolved_sources: HOW MANY ROWS OF METHOD-SOURCES.json NAME NO SOURCE AT ALL, AND IT IS A COUNT PRECISELY SO THAT NO ROW HAS TO BE NAMED. The register admits three source kinds -- a library, a paper by DOI, or a dataset -- and a 'selected' row names exactly one of them. A 'planned' row names none, and tests/test_method_sources.py used to permit that for one row LISTED BY NAME in its own module docstring. A named exception answers for 597 rows and stops answering for the one it names, which is the shape this repository refuses; worse, it hands the next unresolved row a precedent to join in silence. This constant does the same work without the hole: the suite asserts EXACT EQUALITY against it, so a second unresolved row turns that suite red, and resolving the first is a one-line diff here where a reviewer sees it. IT REACHED ZERO ON 2026-08-26, 1 -> 0, WHICH IS THE ONLY TIME THIS CONSTANT HAS MOVED. The row it counted was c00_data_utilities/nber_recession_chronology, whose card describes the NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee's peak/trough chronology -- a published table that no admissible distribution ships and that carries no DOI, so the dataset kind was defined for it. It was resolved by box 2.1.1.2 WITHOUT admitting the table: nber_recessions and nber_recession_flag now take the chronology as a caller-supplied argument, the engine ships nothing and reaches no network, and what remains once the data is the caller's is interval clipping and point-in-interval testing -- date arithmetic, which pandas does. The row is therefore selected on library pandas, wave one, and it resolves as a library row rather than the dataset row it was reserved for. The 2026-08-24 licensing measurement that had blocked it is superseded rather than acted on, and the correction is worth recording so it is not re-derived: the page publishing the chronology carries the line 'Permission to copy is granted, provided attribution of source is given' in its body, so the bytes could have been admitted -- 'All Rights Reserved' is site-wide footer boilerplate, not a claim over that table. The decline is structural, not legal. A ZERO HERE IS NOT A DEAD CONSTANT: the assertion is exact equality, so the first row that ever arrives unresolved turns tests/test_method_sources.py red, which is the work this figure was always doing and which it does best at zero. Reproduce with the command below, run from the engine directory.
engine._comment_undeclared_output_keys: HOW MANY OF THE 1456 NODES HAVE NOT WRITTEN DOWN WHAT THEIR PAYLOAD CONTAINS, AND IT IS A DEBT COUNTER RATHER THAN AN ALLOWLIST -- the same shape and the same reasoning as engine.unresolved_sources above. Until 2026-08-26 nothing in this tree declared a wrapper's payload key set at all: node-specs.json declared argument kinds, the wrapper stub's Returns line said only 'a JSON-safe mapping', and method-cards.json's output_key_fields is prose that describes itself as 'key fields' and may be partial. So every oracle case's key set was a CLAIM the case made ahead of the body rather than a comparison against anything. node-specs.json now carries per-function output_keys, and this counts the nodes whose status is still 'undeclared'. IT MUST REACH ZERO, and the suite asserts EXACT EQUALITY against it, so a node that quietly loses its declaration turns that suite red. WHY THE SEED IS 142 AND NOT 543. 141 of the 600 cards carry exactly one function AND every one of their output_key_fields entries opens with a field name; those 141 can be read mechanically. A further 149 cards parse just as cleanly but carry more than one function between them -- 402 functions -- and copying one card's list onto all of them would assert 402 payload shapes nobody checked. Card 308 is the proof: four clean entries, two functions, and published evidence for exactly one of them. rs_multiple_testing is the single hand-declared addition, because a committed oracle case already asserts its four fields against Benjamini and Hochberg (1995) p. 295. The remaining 626 output_key_fields entries are sentences and are never parsed: a prose sentence turned into a field name by a regular expression is a payload key nobody wrote down. Measured 2026-08-26 by the command below, run from the engine directory.

spdx._comment: TWO VALUES, NOT ONE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM. py_files_total counts the Python files under src/ + scripts/ + tests/; py_files_with_header counts those that declare SPDX-License-Identifier. Asserting both means a file added without a header turns the gate red, where a single figure would simply have moved. This pair is also the one figure a licence change touches everywhere at once, so a reviewer sees it move in a reviewed one-line diff rather than inferring it. It counts a WIDER set than engine.wrappers: alongside the wrapper modules it takes in one __init__.py per wrapper package, the generated tier, the infrastructure modules, the scripts and the tests. engine.test_files is narrower again -- only test_*.py. Reproduce any part by narrowing the py_files_total command below to a single directory; do not restate a breakdown here, because the last one rotted within a day of being written. BOTH FELL BY TWO ON 2026-08-22, together as the pair requires: the replication fixtures were removed by owner decision, and the two Python files that read them went with them. Those two files were written and deleted inside the same uncommitted work, so the commit diff shows neither: what a reviewer sees is the 11 deleted files under engine/fixtures/replications/ and this pair two lower. Each carried an SPDX header, so the two figures moved by the same two files and stayed equal, which is the outcome that proves nothing lost a header in the process. BOTH ROSE BY 28 ON 2026-08-24, together as the pair requires, when the six clusters of box 2.1 merged onto one branch: 783 -> 811, moved by the same files and still equal. The rise breaks down by cluster and the six deltas account for it in full. Boxes 2.1.1/2.1.2/2.1.3 add 2, the register and licence suites; boxes 2.1.15/2.1.12/2.1.11 add 2, the chart-map and serialize suites; boxes 2.1.4/2.1.13 add 13, the five-module gates package with its five suites, tests/support.py and two planted controls; boxes 2.1.6/2.1.5/2.1.7 add 1, the wrapper-generator suite; boxes 2.1.9/2.1.8 add 0, because the oracle cases are JSON; boxes 2.1.14/2.1.16/2.1.17/2.1.18 add 11, ten control modules and the property suite. Those six sum to 29 and the measured rise is 28: engine/tests/controls/__init__.py is authored by two of them and counted once. engine.test_files rose 9 -> 20 across the same merge. BOTH ROSE BY ONE ON 2026-08-29, 827 -> 828, with the second wrapper body: tests/wrappers/c16_limited_dependent/test_count_models.py is the only Python file the change adds, and engine.test_files rose 30 -> 31 with it. The three published tables it reaches for are JSON under tests/fixtures/ and are counted by neither figure.
spdx._comment_min_scanned: THE ANTI-VACUITY FLOOR FOR ci.yml's SPDX SCAN, AND A DIFFERENT QUANTITY FROM py_files_total. That pair is an exact-equality assertion; this is a floor whose only job is to prove the loop scanned a whole tree rather than a fragment. It lived as a literal `-lt 740` inside .github/workflows/ci.yml, which made it the one asserted quantity with a second home -- harmless while the tree is far above it, and not harmless the day somebody lowers a number. It is read from here now, by the same python3 -c form every other floor in that workflow uses. WHY 740 AND NOT SOMETHING ELSE: it sits BELOW the 811 the glob matches today and ABOVE the 715 that remain if the generated tier is ever dropped from the glob by accident, so losing a whole tier turns the scan red -- the one thing a floor placed below 715 could not do. Both figures, from engine/: `find src scripts tests -name '*.py' -not -path '*__pycache__*' | wc -l` and the same command with `-not -path 'src/econflow_engine/generated/*'` added.

artifacts._comment: COUNTS OF THE COMMITTED ARTIFACTS. n_nodes, n_categories and n_cards describe the LIVE catalogue and move when it grows -- they are measurements, not promises. n_legacy_nodes and n_legacy_cards describe the contract that was retired on 2026-08-21 and are read from legacy-inventory.json; they must NEVER move, because a continuity constant that drifts was never one. Until that date the live pair was asserted under _v2 names beside a frozen pair under the plain names, and after the merge both read the same file and contradicted each other. n_parity_cases and n_recommend_fixtures describe frozen oracles and do not move either. THE VALUE "unmeasured" IS A HARD FAILURE, NOT A PLACEHOLDER: it marks a constant whose measuring artifact is not in the tree yet, and assert.sh fails loudly and names it.

boundary._comment: backend/ declares no dependency of its own, and THAT is the assertion. The engine-boundary gate used to report that it examined zero specifiers and pass, which is indistinguishable from a detector that stopped working. Zero here is a MEASURED figure, not an unset default: the gate fails outright if this key is missing, and the comparison is EXACT, so the first dependency the platform layer ever takes turns the gate red until this number is moved in a reviewed one-line diff.

docs._comment: FLOORS, not exact counts, and each one sits BELOW what its command returns. Re-baselined 2026-08-22, after the published documentation set was cut to README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md. Everything else -- the decision records, the layer READMEs, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, SECURITY, PROVENANCE and the generated category guides -- was deleted because the project documents far more than it does: nothing computes yet. Measured 2026-08-22 by the commands below, which are the only figures that count: min_markdown_files returns 3, min_links_checked returns 5, min_doc_claims returns 14. THE MARKDOWN COUNT IS 3, NOT 2, AND THE EARLIER COMMENT HERE CONTRADICTED ITS OWN COMMAND. `git ls-files '*.md'` also finds .github/vale/styles/proselint/README.md, the README of the vendored errata-ai style, which is tracked and which vale lints like any other file. The floor stays at 2 and must not be raised to meet the measurement: it answers for the published set, while the vendored README arrives and leaves with an upstream sync that has nothing to say about this repository's documentation. The link total moves with ordinary content for the same reason, which is why 3 rather than 5. A floor below its measurement still refuses the one failure these exist for -- a gate that quietly stopped examining the tree -- whereas a floor set to equality turns an ordinary content change into a red gate and teaches people to edit the number.

secrets._comment: A FLOOR ON WORK DONE, not on findings. trufflehog exits 0 whether it scanned the tree or nothing at all, and --only-verified means a clean run is the EXPECTED outcome -- so the exit code carries almost no information and the chunk count carries all of it. Measured 2026-08-20 against a clean export of the tracked tree (30 MB, what a CI checkout actually holds): 3504 chunks. The floor is set well below that because the figure moves with ordinary content, and its job is to catch a scan that examined a handful of files, not to track the tree.

suite._comment: min_tests is a floor, deliberately. The suite total moves upward as tests are added and must never move DOWN unnoticed, which is what this floor catches; failed and error are exact. The figure is low because every method handler is still a typed stub that raises, and a handler's tests land with its implementation -- the conformance harness, the argument-contract harness and the contract-hash suite are the only suites that exist yet. It rises as the per-wrapper suites land, and it is lowered only when the tests it counted are themselves deleted, in a diff that says so and names them. Each rise so far was its own reviewed diff: 73 -> 103 by the contract-hash suite, 103 -> 132 by the corpus and gen_artifacts suite, 132 -> 143 by the index-label suite, 143 -> 149 by the thread-pinning suite, all on 2026-08-20. The value below is higher than 149 and the step that took it there was never recorded here; record the next one. The pyright narrowings brought tests of their own: serialize.py and chart_spec.py had no test of any kind when their missing-stamp guards were rewritten to satisfy a type checker. THIS FLOOR MOVED DOWN ON 2026-08-22, 163 -> 139, FOR THE FIRST TIME. The replication fixtures under engine/fixtures/replications/ were removed by owner decision, and the 24 tests that read them went with them. That test module was written and deleted inside the same uncommitted work, so a reviewer sees the 11 deleted fixture files and no test module beside them. A floor left at 163 would then refuse every run of a suite that is complete, which is the opposite of what it exists for. The new value measures the whole collected suite after that removal: the command below returns 139, and engine.test_files fell from 10 to 9 in the same change. IT ROSE TO 633 ON 2026-08-28, AND THE STEP THAT MATTERS IS THE DRIFT IT CLOSES RATHER THAN THE FOUR TESTS THAT PROMPTED IT. The floor stood at 594 while the suite collected 629, so thirty-five tests could have been deleted before this gate said anything -- the gap opened because every change after 2.2.5 added tests without moving the floor, which is the movement this constant exists to notice. It is set to the collected count again, measured by the command below over the branch tip: 629 before, 633 after. The four are tests/test_annotation_resolution.py, which proves that a wrapper signature naming pd or np resolves at CALL time and not only for a type checker. That is the one defect no static gate in this tree can see: beartype resolves a signature's annotations when a body is called, and 536 of the 598 wrapper modules named those types behind if TYPE_CHECKING, so gen_wrappers --check, ruff, mypy, pyright and lint-imports were all green over it. Two of the four are planted controls run in one subprocess, one per header shape; the third parses all 598 wrapper modules and, for the 536 that name pd or np anywhere in a signature, imports the module and looks the annotated name up in its real namespace -- the other 62 annotate neither, so they hold no forward reference that could fail to resolve; the fourth calls the 522 wrapper functions whose required parameters are handles alone, across 295 modules, and requires each to reach its NotImplementedError. Both sweeps were watched failing against the pre-fix tier before they were trusted. THE COLLECTED COUNT IS A SAFE FLOOR HERE, AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The suite has exactly one skip site -- a pytest.skip inside tests/conformance/test_conformance.py, taken when a case names a body that is not implemented yet -- and a run-time skip does not change what pytest COLLECTS. There is no skipif, no importorskip and no collect_ignore anywhere under tests/, so collection is invariant both to how many bodies are implemented and to the machine; three consecutive runs under three pytest-randomly seeds returned 633. engine.test_files rose 29 -> 30 and the spdx pair 826 -> 827, all three moved by the same one new module. IT ROSE TO 634 ON 2026-08-29, BY ONE TEST, AND THE SENTENCES ABOVE HAD TO BE CORRECTED IN THE SAME DIFF -- WHICH IS THE PART WORTH READING. tests/test_annotation_resolution.py gains test_the_session_hook_is_live_over_the_wrapper_tier: it calls a wrapper with a deliberately wrong argument type and requires beartype's BeartypeCallHintParamViolation. The two planted controls cannot answer that question and never could. They run in a CHILD interpreter that installs its own beartype_package over its own planted package, so they are blind to this session's hook: commenting out beartype_package("econflow_engine") in engine/tests/conftest.py left all four tests green while the sweeps had stopped reaching beartype at all, and the call sweep was then vacuous, because a stub raises NotImplementedError with or without the hook. Watched failing that way, then conftest.py restored byte for byte. THE NAMESPACE SWEEP'S DENOMINATOR WAS OVERSTATED HERE FROM THE DAY IT WAS WRITTEN. It kept only annotations on REQUIRED parameters, so it examined 521 of 598 modules rather than every one, and never opened the fifteen that import pandas or numpy for an OPTIONAL parameter alone -- where the defect was live, because beartype resolves that annotation the moment the optional argument is passed. It sweeps every annotation now, required or optional, and examines 536. Neither meaningful figure was floored anywhere -- either sweep could have shrunk to one and stayed green -- and both are floored now, as suite.min_signature_name_modules and suite.min_handle_only_calls, each watched failing against a planted shrink. suite._comment_annotation_sweeps: THE TWO DENOMINATORS OF engine/tests/test_annotation_resolution.py, AND THE REASON THEY ARE CONSTANTS RATHER THAN PROSE. That module floors only `parsed >= engine.wrappers`, which counts FILES WALKED and is satisfied by walking all 598 and examining none of them; the two figures that say how much was actually examined were bare `> 0` assertions, so either sweep could have shrunk to a single module and stayed green while the paragraph here still claimed 598. min_signature_name_modules counts the wrapper modules naming pd or np ANYWHERE in a signature, required parameter or optional -- 536 of 598, and the remaining 62 annotate neither, so no forward reference in them can fail to resolve. min_handle_only_calls counts the call sites whose required parameters are all pandas or numpy handles, which is the set the call sweep can build arguments for: 522 of them, across 295 modules. THE FIRST FIGURE WAS 521 UNTIL 2026-08-29, AND THE FIFTEEN IT MISSED WERE THE DEFECT THIS PAIR EXISTS TO CATCH. The sweep filtered to REQUIRED parameters, so fifteen modules that import pandas or numpy for an optional parameter alone were never opened -- and beartype resolves that annotation the moment the optional argument is passed, so the wall was live on every one of them. Both are floors and not equalities: a wrapper added to the catalogue raises them, and must not turn the suite red for it. Either is lowered only in a diff that names the modules or the call sites it counted. Measured 2026-08-29 by the commands below.
suite._comment_min_oracle_cases: A FLOOR ON ORACLE CASES THAT RAN, not on cases that exist. The oracle harness compares a node's payload against a published number, and every wrapper body is a stub -- so a corpus of node cases alone skips in full and reports success while comparing nothing. That is the shape of gate this repository refuses, and it is why the floor counts EXECUTION rather than files. It is met today by cases against the engine's own already-written helpers, under engine/tests/oracle/engine/, which is what the command below counts: every case in that namespace runs, because the code it calls exists. The measured figure rises as wrapper bodies land and their cases start running, and the floor rises with it in a reviewed one-line diff. It is lowered only when the cases it counted are themselves deleted, in a diff that names them.
suite._comment_min_fixture_cases: THE ANTI-VACUITY FLOOR FOR THE FIXTURE FORM, AND IT IS NON-ZERO ON THE DAY THAT FORM LANDS. An oracle case names its inputs as JSON literals, which reaches 103 of the 1456 nodes; the other 1353 take a handle or a path. A {"$fixture": "<name>"} value inside `inputs` builds a published table from engine/tests/fixtures/ and substitutes it -- as a registry handle in the wrapper namespace, so run_method is called unchanged and validate_wire, adapt_args, resolve_handle and _AS_KIND all run, and as the object itself in the engine namespace. WHY A FLOOR OF ZERO WOULD HAVE BEEN VACUOUS, which is the whole reason this constant exists: every wrapper body is a stub, so every wrapper-namespace fixture case reports not-implemented and skips, and a floor of zero over that corpus is satisfied by a form that has never once built an object. The engine namespace closes it -- a to_mcp case over the Anscombe (1973) frame runs today and compares eleven published pairs against a payload whose column-to-value pairing the dataset file does not contain in that form. RAISE IT as fixture cases land; lower it only in a diff that names the cases it counted. Asserted inside the harness rather than in assert.sh, which flattens only the engine|spdx|artifacts|suite sections and cannot know which cases RAN rather than skipped -- the same siting as min_oracle_cases above and oracle.literal_callable_nodes. Measured 2026-08-26 by the command below.
suite._comment_fixture_controls: THE PLANTED CONTROLS IN engine/tests/controls/fixture_reach.py, ASSERTED BY EXACT EQUALITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Node-shaped callables are driven through the REAL registry_put -> adapt_args -> resolve_handle path against a real node's contract. Two must be flagged: a callable that ignores its handle argument and returns a constant, and one whose payload does not move when the dataset's values move. Two must NOT be: one that reads the data, and one whose payload legitimately does not depend on the values and declares itself as such. A positive control that goes unflagged means this check cannot detect a body ignoring its input at all; a negative control that gets flagged means it has decayed into a rule that refuses correct code. Those are different defects and the module reports them separately, exactly as double_run.py does. Measured 2026-08-26 by the command below.
suite._comment_controls: THE THREE PLANTED-CONTROL COUNTS, ADDED 2026-08-23 WITH BOXES 2.1.14, 2.1.16 AND 2.1.18. All three harnesses are written against implemented wrapper bodies, and engine.n_implemented is 0 -- so run as written each would examine nothing and report success, which is the failure ARCHITECTURE.md 11.1 exists to refuse and which this tree has hit six times. Each therefore carries planted positive controls it MUST flag and negative controls it MUST NOT, on the pattern .github/scripts/check-no-network.sh established. These counts are EXACT, not floors: deleting a control must be a visible one-line diff here, because a harness silently left with fewer controls than it claims is indistinguishable from one that has stopped proving itself. The wrapper-facing floors are separate and read engine.n_implemented, so they rise on their own with the first body in 2.2 and need no second edit. NOTE these are NOT checked by assert-inventory/assert.sh: it flattens the engine|spdx|artifacts|suite sections but only compares the keys it names explicitly, exactly as it already leaves min_tests, failed and error to run_verifications.sh. The measuring sites are steps 11, 12 and 13 of engine/run_verifications.sh.

oracle._comment: HOW FAR AN ORACLE CASE CAN REACH, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A COMMENT. A case file names its inputs as JSON literals, so it can call a node only where no REQUIRED argument of that node needs something a file cannot hold: a handle produced by an earlier node, or the ticket name of an uploaded dataset. Every other node needs a fixture before a case can reach it, and building those fixtures is its own box -- this constant is what makes that gap countable rather than a sentence somebody wrote once. Measured 2026-08-24 by the command below: 103 of the 1456 nodes, leaving 1353 that a case cannot reach today. It is asserted in engine/tests/conformance/test_conformance.py and NOT in assert-inventory/assert.sh, which flattens only the engine|spdx|artifacts|suite sections; the harness is the right measuring site because the harness is what the number describes. THE BLOCKED SET IS READ FROM node-specs.json rather than typed into either home: vocabulary.pointer_handle_kinds is the contract's own list, and a second copy would be free to drift from it in silence. `path` is added to it because a path names a dataset somebody uploaded, which a case file cannot hold either. A DROP IN THIS NUMBER IS NEWS: it means the catalogue moved a node behind a handle, and the oracle corpus lost somewhere it could go.

image._comment: A CEILING AND A FLOOR, AND THE FLOOR IS THE HALF THAT CANNOT BE SKIPPED. A ceiling alone passes on an image that failed to build and inspects as 0 bytes, which is the vacuous-gate shape ARCHITECTURE.md 11.1 forbids -- so the size must also be ABOVE a figure only a real image reaches. THIS SECTION IS INERT IN assert-inventory/assert.sh BY DESIGN: that script flattens only the engine, spdx, artifacts and suite sections, and it runs on a laptop with no image built. The measuring site is the `full` path of .github/workflows/engine-suite.yml, which builds the image and reads both bounds from here with NO default -- a missing key fails the step rather than falling back to a number nobody reviewed. baseline_bytes is the last measurement, recorded so a reviewer can see how much headroom the ceiling actually leaves; it is not asserted, because the image size moves with every base-image and wheel update. It reads 611923959, printed by that step on 2026-08-24 in engine-suite run 32749030661: `image size 611923959 bytes (floor 314572800, ceiling 1073741824)`. TAKE THE FIGURE FROM THE RUNNER AND NOT FROM A WORKSTATION, because `docker image inspect --format '{{.Size}}'` does not measure one thing. Docker 29 with the containerd image store enabled (`Storage Driver: overlayfs`) reports the COMPRESSED content size; the runner's classic store reports the sum of the UNCOMPRESSED layer sizes, and the gate above compares that. The same runtime image measured 539430818 on a containerd-store laptop and 1786165749 on the runner, a factor of 3.3 -- so a baseline recorded from the smaller number describes headroom the gate does not see. That reading is also why the layer sum is what a Dockerfile must economise: a recursive chown after a COPY emits a second copy of every byte, and both copies are charged. The ceiling is 1 GiB and the floor 300 MiB, both round numbers chosen as bounds rather than measurements: Galaxy pulls this image per job, and an engine that doubles in size is a change somebody must argue for.

commands.py_files_with_header: find src scripts tests -name '*.py' -not -path '*__pycache__*' -print0 | xargs -0 grep -l 'SPDX-License-Identifier' | wc -l
commands.min_tests: python3 -m pytest --collect-only -q | tail -1 | sed 's/ tests\? collected.*//'
commands.image_baseline_bytes: docker build --no-cache --target runtime -t econflow-engine:ci .. && docker image inspect econflow-engine:ci --format '{{.Size}}'
commands.unresolved_sources: python3 -c "import json;print(sum(1 for r in json.load(open('METHOD-SOURCES.json'))['modules'].values() if not (r['library'] or r['paper'] or r['dataset'])))"
commands.undeclared_output_keys: python3 -c "import json;print(sum(1 for n in json.load(open('artifacts/node-specs.json'))['nodes'] if n['output_keys']['status'] == 'undeclared'))"
commands.literal_callable_nodes: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('artifacts/node-specs.json'));b=set(d['vocabulary']['pointer_handle_kinds'])|{'path'};print(sum(1 for n in d['nodes'] if not any(a['kind'] in b for a in n['arguments'] if a['required'])))"
commands.mutation_min_mutants: uv run --project .. mutmut run >/dev/null 2>&1; uv run --project .. mutmut export-cicd-stats >/dev/null && python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('mutants/mutmut-cicd-stats.json'))['total'])"

_note_on_grep: py_files_with_header uses find -print0 | xargs -0 grep -l, NOT grep -rl --include.
On a maintainer machine `grep` resolves to ugrep, which under 7.5.0 read
--include differently and silently undercounted the tree. CONTRIBUTING.md
carries that measurement and both commands; it also records that 7.8.4 fixed
the behaviour. The rule stands: a gate written with --include undercounts on
an older host and passes in CI, which is the failure direction CONTRIBUTING.md
forbids -- the gate goes green locally while missing files.

skill_refs._comment: Floor for check-skill-citations.sh. THE DENOMINATOR IS CITATIONS RESOLVED, not citations matched, and the difference is the whole point: the counter used to increment on every backticked path-shaped match and the loop then skipped placeholders, slash commands, the git-ignored names and other projects' files -- 104 counted against 80 actually resolved. A skill rewritten with placeholder paths throughout would have cleared the floor while resolving nothing, which is the exact vacuity a floor exists to refuse. The counter now increments inside judge(), only for a citation that reaches resolve(). Measured 2026-08-26 over the econflow-wrapper skill: 80 resolved across SKILL.md and its six references. The floor sits below that with room for ordinary editing and far above the collapse this must catch, a walk that reached one document instead of seven. NOTE THE ONE WAY THIS GATE CANNOT RUN, and it is stated in the script rather than hidden: the skills are ignored by git, so a clone and every CI job hold none of them and the script exits 0 after saying it examined nothing.

private_refs._comment: Floor for check-private-refs.sh, which reads the TRACKED set from git's index rather than walking the filesystem, so its denominator is `git ls-files | wc -l` and not the vocabulary gate's figure. A floor, not an exact count: tracked files come and go with ordinary work, and the only failure this must refuse is a scan whose walk collapsed. Measured 2026-08-23: 962 tracked files, all of them text-decodable and therefore all examined. The floor sits well below that. NOTE THE ONE WAY THIS READS LOW HONESTLY -- a file that is tracked but deleted in the working tree cannot be read and is not counted, so an unstaged deletion lowers the figure without lowering the tree.

vocabulary._comment: Floor for check-vocabulary.sh. A floor, not an exact count: files come and go constantly, and the only thing this must catch is a scan that stopped examining the tree. Measured 2026-08-21: 1056 files examined, so the floor sits well below the measurement and still refuses a scan whose walk collapsed.

mutation._comment: BOX 2.1.17 -- MUTATION TESTING, NIGHTLY ONLY, AND INERT IN assert.sh BY DESIGN. assert-inventory/assert.sh flattens only the engine|spdx|artifacts|suite sections, so nothing here is read there; the measuring site is the `mutation` job in .github/workflows/engine-suite.yml and nowhere else. That is deliberate: a mutmut run rebuilds the tree under mutants/ and re-runs the suite once per surviving mutant, which is minutes rather than the three seconds run_verifications.sh takes, and it must never become a ci-gate leaf -- ci-gate asserts exactly 12 results at ci.yml:1685 and check-required-contexts.sh cross-checks the needs list. min_mutants IS THE ANTI-VACUITY ASSERTION AND IT IS CHECKED FIRST, BEFORE ANY KILL RATE IS READ: zero mutants over an empty or mistyped path yields 0 killed of 0 generated, which every naive formula reports as a 100 % kill rate -- a perfect score for having tested nothing. min_kill_rate IS MEASURED, NEVER GUESSED. The figure below is low and is recorded honestly: serialize.py and chart_spec.py have almost no direct test coverage beyond tests/test_index_labels.py and the property tests added in 2.1.16. A floor invented above the measurement is a gate that fails on arrival; one invented below it is decorative. Raise it when the tests that justify it land, in a diff that names them.
mutation._comment_measured: MEASURED 2026-08-24 over serialize.py, chart_spec.py and gates/primitives.py together, by the two commands in the 'commands' block, on the merged 2.1 tree: total 939, killed 536, survived 394, no_tests 9 -- a kill rate of 57.1 %. THE BASIS IS WIDER THAN THE LAST MEASUREMENT AND THE FIGURES ARE NOT COMPARABLE WITH IT: that one ran over two modules and this one runs over three, and the third arrives with the five gate suites box 2.1.4 wrote for it, which is where most of the rise comes from. THE FLOORS BELOW SIT UNDER THOSE FIGURES AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. min_mutants is 600 against 939 measured: the mutant count moves with any ordinary edit to three files, and this floor's job is to refuse a run that collapsed to zero, not to track the tree. min_kill_rate is 57.0 against 57.1 measured, which is as close as an honest floor gets: a floor invented ABOVE the measurement is a gate that fails on arrival, and one invented far below it is decorative. 394 survivors is not a good number and is not presented as one -- each is a change to one of the three modules that no test objects to. Raise this floor when the tests that justify it land, in a diff that names them, and never to make a red nightly green. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-26 UNDER BOXES 2.1.1.6 AND 2.1.1.7, AND THE FIGURE DID NOT MOVE: total 939, killed 536, survived 394, no_tests 9 -- 57.1 % again, read from mutants/mutmut-cicd-stats.json rather than from mutmut's exit code. THE BASIS DID MOVE AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS HERE: the deselect list in engine/pyproject.toml fell from 22 selectors to 3, so 459 tests now judge every mutant against the 340 recorded above, measured by running the suite from inside engine/mutants/ with the committed selection, which reported '459 passed, 1 skipped, 8 deselected' and no failures. THAT THE RATE IS UNCHANGED OVER A BASIS A THIRD LARGER IS ITSELF THE RESULT, and it confirms by measurement what the previous comment asserted: the twenty harnesses that came back all assert agreement with this manifest or with the environment rather than a numerical answer, so none of them can kill a mutant of the three target modules. THE PREVIOUS FIGURE WAS NOT REPRODUCIBLE ON THIS BRANCH AT ALL, which is why this re-measurement was not optional: at 0100fb0 a baseline run inside mutants/ reported '14 failed, 420 passed, 1 skipped, 27 deselected', so mutmut aborted before generating a mutant and the nightly job could not have produced any rate. Thirteen of the fourteen were harnesses that adopted the ENGINE_ROOT.parent manifest read after the list was last measured on 2026-08-24. The floors below are unchanged and stay under the measurement: min_kill_rate 57.0 against 57.1, min_mutants 600 against 939.
mutation._comment_targets: THIS LIST AND `[tool.mutmut] only_mutate` IN engine/pyproject.toml NAME THE SAME THREE PATHS, and the figures above are measured over exactly that set. Adding a path in one home without re-measuring leaves both floors describing a tree that is not the one being mutated, so the two move in one diff. The mutation job skips a target that is absent and SAYS SO, and turns red if EVERY target is absent. A FOURTH FACT BELONGS HERE BECAUSE IT BOUNDS WHAT THESE FIGURES MEAN: mutmut runs the suite from engine/mutants/, which inserts one directory level, so every harness locating this manifest as ENGINE_ROOT.parent / '.github' / 'inventory.json' resolves ABOVE the sandbox and cannot execute there. The 24 tests that fail for that reason, plus tests/test_thread_pinning.py and one beartype/trampoline interaction, are deselected in [tool.mutmut] by a MEASURED list -- the exact set a baseline run inside mutants/ reports -- and 340 tests still judge every mutant. Each deselected harness runs in full on every commit through run_verifications.sh and assert-inventory/assert.sh.
